n: The last of Asaph’s psalms opens with an urgent plea: God, don’t stay silent or still while your people are threatened.
God’s enemies are in an uproar and raising their heads in defiance.
They plot craftily against God’s people — those he treasures and protects.
Their goal is total destruction: wipe Israel off the map so its name is forgotten.

f.w: let us cut them off from being a nation

n: They have united in one mind, forming an alliance — not just against Israel but against God himself.
The list of enemies surrounds Israel: Edom, the desert Ishmaelites, Moab, and the Hagrites east of the Jordan.

f.g: Hagrites, a tribe east of the Jordan, possibly descended from Hagar.

n: More foes: Gebal (Byblos or a region near Edom), Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines and Tyre.

f.g: Either Byblos on the coast of Lebanon or a region south of the Dead Sea.
Israel’s ancient enemy from the Exodus.

n: Even Assyria has joined, lending strength to Moab and Ammon, Lot’s descendants. No single historical alliance matches this list exactly; it may gather Israel’s enemies from many eras.
Do to them what you did in the days of the judges — to Midian under Gideon, and to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River under Deborah and Barak.

f.g: The Kishon River in the Jezreel Valley.

n: They died at En-dor and lay on the ground like manure.

f.g: A town near Mount Tabor, close to where Sisera’s army fell.

n: Treat their leaders like the Midianite princes Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna, whom Gideon defeated.
These are the ones who said, “Let’s take God’s pastures for ourselves.”

f.g: God’s pasturelands — the land of Israel.

n: Make them like tumbleweed blown by the wind, like straw in a gale.

f.g: Leftover dry stalks — light and worthless.

n: As fire sweeps through a forest and flames set mountains ablaze...
...so pursue them with your storm and terrify them with your hurricane.
An important twist: cover them with shame “that they may seek thy name.” The deeper goal is not destruction but repentance.

f.w: that they may seek thy name

n: Let them be disgraced and dismayed forever if they won’t turn.

The purpose of it all: that the world will know that you alone, whose name is Jehovah, are Most High over the earth. This is one of the few places the KJV spells out the divine name. Latter-day Saints understand Jehovah as the premortal Christ.

f.g: An English form of YHWH, God’s covenant name, usually printed “LORD” in the KJV.
